summary: Prefabricated 1950 Weyerhaeuser lookout on a 10 ft tower in the Umpqua NF; restored, reported staffed, reached by a gated road walk, with a 2024 closure notice on one post.

facts.design: prefabricated L-4-type cab on a 10 ft wooden tower (cab size disputed: 10x10 ft or 14x14 ft)

staffing.status: staffed by volunteers (firelookout.com; 2023 visitor found it marked Staffed)

access.note: On a July 2, 2022 visit a locked gate on the access road blocked vehicles, and visitors walked about a mile from it. The 2022 post says vandals had cut the gate and a Forest Service crew seemed to have recently fixed it. A notice on that post says the area was closed as of July 20, 2024, due to the active Diamond Complex; no source read says when it reopened. No rentals are mentioned in the sources.

visit.trail_note: Reach the gate by the Mowich Loop Road and NF-100, then walk about a mile. A 2023 visitor also came by a trail from Road 250. Pig Iron Trail #1438 is reported as overgrown and steep.

events.note: Prefabricated by the Weyerhaeuser Sales Company; the current structure was built into the fall of 1950.
Dwight Berryman lived in a tent; the fire finder stood outdoors under a cover when not in use.
Mainly staffed during the afternoon hours. Former lookout Gary Wilson says he manned it that summer.
An August 4, 1962 News-Review item, under Staffing, names Russell Dondero, a Roseburg resident who attends Whitman College.
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register on March 1, 2000.

corrections.why: Both the Register and firelookout.com describe a 10 ft wooden tower, which is 3.0 m. The record's 4.3 m (about 14 ft) matches neither; it may be the 14 ft cab dimension that firelookout.com gives.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register gives a 10 by 10 ft cab; firelookout.com and the Oregon Lookouts history give 14 by 14 ft. The record gives no cab size, and the story reports both figures.

The Register puts the lookout a half mile below the summit; firelookout.com says one mile west; the 2023 visitor says a little west of the actual summit. The story gives the Register and firelookout.com figures.
The Register gives 4,828 ft (1,472 m); firelookout.com gives 4881 ft. The record's 1471.6 m matches the Register.
Firelookout.com calls it staffed by volunteers; the 2022 Roaming Civic post describes the attendant as employed through the Forest Service. The story attributes each description to its source.

A locked gate on the access road was reported in July 2022; a 2023 visitor walked in on the Road 250 trail; a closure notice dated as of July 20, 2024 appears on the 2022 post. No source read says whether the area reopened.

notes_for_editor: Coordinates disagree: the Register gives N 43.264680, W 122.264680, while the record's longitude of -122.37989 (and 43.2642 latitude) differs by about 0.11 degrees, roughly 9 km. Not resolved in the record; the editor should check the coordinates against the Register and a map before any change. Current status rests on a 2023 visitor report and the undated Roaming Civic post; no 2025-26 source read. Forest Service trail page and an FFLA Facebook post were seen in search but not read. The 1950 and 1951 staffing items and the 1962 News-Review item are only as transcribed on oregonlookouts.weebly.com; originals not checked. Photos not added: no image URLs or licenses confirmed.
